01 . This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
Heard Mr. Juliyas Prasad Behera, learned counsel for the petitioners and Mr.Ray, learned counsel for the State.

This writ petition has been filed by the petitioners with a prayer to quash the notice dated 05.04.2025 passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Shalagaon-Budapank-Talcher- Jarapada, opposite party no.5.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the case land relates to Khata No.345, Plot no.336,
Kisam-Gharbari, Ac.0.09 dec. and for acquisition of such land, the petitioners have received a sum of Rs.26,00,000/- including solatium on 28.03.2023 and though the Authorities have quantified Rs.7,00,000/- to be paid for rehabilitation and resettlement packages, but the petitioners have two shares in that amount, but no notice has been issued to the petitioners.
On the other hand, a demolition notice under Annexure-11 has been issued wherein it is stated that the authorities will demolish the structure and acquire the land today, i.e., on 11.04.2025.

Referring to section 31 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 Act (hereinafter referred to as 2013 Act), learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the said provision provides that the Collector is to pass rehabilitation and resettlement award for each of the affected family in terms of entitlements provided in the second schedule.

Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 Act

sentences.text: He further placed section 38 of the 2013 Act wherein it is stated that the Collector shall take possession of the land after ensuring that full payment of compensation as well as rehabilitation and resettlement entitlements are paid or tendered to the entitled persons within a period of three months for the compensation and period of six months for the monetary part of rehabilitation and resettlement entitlements listed in the second schedule and sub-section (2) of section 38 states that the Collector shall be responsible for ensuring that rehabilitation and resettlement process is completed in all respect before displacing the affected families.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that when the petitioners have been paid a sum of Rs.26,00,000/- on 28.03.2023 for the acquisition of the land for the self-same land,
they should not have been deprived of the rehabilitation and resettlement entitlements and the action of the authorities is per se illegal.
Section 64 of the 2013 Act deals with reference to the Authorities and it states as follows:-
"Reference to Authority- (1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Authority, as the case may be where his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the persons to whom it is payable, the rights of Rehabilitation and Resettlement under Chapter V and VI or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested:
Provided that the Collector shall, within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of application, make a reference to the appropriate Authority:
Provided further that where the Collector fails to make such reference within the period so specified, the applicant may apply to the Authority, as the case may be,
requesting it to direct the Collector to make the reference to it within a period of thirty days.
(2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:
Provided that every such application shall be made- (a) If the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collector's award;
(b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 21, or within six months from the date of the Collector's award,

Provided further that the Collector may entertain an application after the expiry of the said period,
within a further period of one year, if he is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for not filling it within the period specified in the first proviso."

In view of such provision, since alternative remedy for availing a share in the quantified amount of Rs.7,00,000/- as per Annexures-3 and 9 are available with the petitioners, this writ petition is disposed of giving them liberty to avail such remedy in accordance with law.
With such observation, the writ petition stands disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy as per Rules.
